page: Microsoft Azure FX32-16mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 672.0 GB, translating to 42.0 GB of RAM per core. The configuration also includes 1890 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, while containing zero GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the FX32-16mds_v2 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring 2315.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and showing strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.78 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.22 GB/sec. Its memory subsystem delivers a strong write bandwidth of 91.91 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a top-tier text processing score of 2959.0. Multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, align with average middle-tier performance, reflecting the 16-vCPU hardware limit despite the high individual core frequency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, providing a massive memory footprint relative to its vCPU count. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, and text-processing tasks that benefit from high single-core clock speeds and substantial RAM. However, for highly parallelized multi-threaded compute tasks, the 16-vCPU limit represents a tradeoff compared to higher-core alternatives.
